title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: jvecfor high-performance KNN library Bioconductor single-cell workflows. wraps Java library, built top jvector, implements two algorithms: HNSW-DiskANN (type = "ann") – approximate KNN via Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs, SIMD-accelerated distance computation (AVX2/AVX-512). O(log n) query time; ~2× faster BiocNeighbors n ≥ 100K cells. VP-tree (type = "knn") — exact KNN using vantage-point trees. Deterministic; ideal small datasets ground-truth validation. R package communicates JVM via system2() — JNI, rJava dependency. JAR bundled inst/java/ requires separate installation step beyond Java 20+ PATH.

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: output fastFindKNN() named list $index (n × k integer matrix, 1-based) $distance (n × k numeric matrix), identical structure BiocNeighbors::findKNN().

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: jvecfor requires Java ≥ 20 PATH. JAR uses jdk.incubator.vector module SIMD acceleration. Check installation: java found, install Eclipse Temurin OpenJDK 20+ distribution ensure java binary PATH. JAVA_HOME set, jvecfor tries $JAVA_HOME/bin/java first uses whichever java PATH Java 20 newer.
code: system2("java", "--version")  # should print openjdk 20 or higher

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: Two global options control runtime behaviour: Set persistently .Rprofile per-session:
code: options(jvecfor.verbose = TRUE)                        # global verbose mode options(jvecfor.jar = "/path/to/custom/jvecfor.jar")   # custom JAR

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: bundled JAR installed automatically. compiled custom jvecfor build:
code: # Auto-finds target/jvecfor-*.jar relative to the working directory jvecfor_setup()  # Or provide the path explicitly jvecfor_setup(jar_path = "/path/to/jvecfor-x.y.z.jar")

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: result two-element list. $index 300 × 15 integer matrix 1-based neighbor indices; $distance 300 × 15 numeric matrix Euclidean distances.
code: library(jvecfor)  # Simulate 300 cells × 30 principal components set.seed(42) pca <- matrix(rnorm(300 * 30), nrow = 300, ncol = 30)  # Find 15 nearest neighbours (HNSW-DiskANN approximate, Euclidean) nn <- fastFindKNN(pca, k = 15)  str(nn) #> List of 2 #>  $ index   : int [1:300, 1:15] 271 263 125 158 271 241 210 2 153 235 ... #>   ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2 #>   .. ..$ : NULL #>   .. ..$ : chr [1:15] "V1" "V2" "V3" "V4" ... #>  $ distance: num [1:300, 1:15] 0.0508 0.0396 0.0471 0.0409 0.0331 ... #>   ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2 #>   .. ..$ : NULL #>   .. ..$ : chr [1:15] "V16" "V17" "V18" "V19" ...

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: output structurally identical BiocNeighbors::findKNN(), existing code passes nn$index bluster Bioconductor tools works without modification.
code: dim(nn$index)     # 300 x 15 #> [1] 300  15 dim(nn$distance)  # 300 x 15 #> [1] 300  15  class(nn$index)     # "integer" — 1-based, same as BiocNeighbors #> [1] "matrix" "array" class(nn$distance)  # "numeric" #> [1] "matrix" "array"  # No zeros in index (1-based) and all values within [1, nrow(pca)] range(nn$index) #> [1]   1 298

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: choose ANN vs. exact:
code: # Approximate (HNSW-DiskANN) — default, fast, O(log n) query nn_ann <- fastFindKNN(pca, k = 15, type = "ann")  # Exact (VP-tree) — deterministic, O(n log n) query nn_knn <- fastFindKNN(pca, k = 15, type = "knn")  # Self-consistency check: exact search always returns itself as nearest # (excluding self) — no duplicate indices per row stopifnot(all(apply(nn_knn$index, 1, function(x) !anyDuplicated(x))))

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: L2 distance PC space. Appropriate principal components whitened (equal variance per component) embedding preserves meaningful inter-cell distances.
code: nn_euc <- fastFindKNN(pca, k = 15, metric = "euclidean")

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: Measures angle cell vectors; ignores magnitude. useful direction embedding vector matters, instance log-normalised count embeddings library-size effects inflate norms. Normalise rows unit length calling ensure consistent behaviour:
code: # L2-normalise rows norms    <- sqrt(rowSums(pca^2)) pca_norm <- sweep(pca, 1, norms, "/")  nn_cos <- fastFindKNN(pca_norm, k = 15, metric = "cosine")

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: inner product ⟨u, v⟩. similarity measure (higher = similar) rather distance. valid type = "ann" — VP-tree requires proper metric. Attempting combine metric = "dot_product" type = "knn" raises informative error:
code: # ANN with dot-product similarity nn_dot <- fastFindKNN(pca_norm, k = 15, metric = "dot_product", type = "ann") # Attempting exact + dot_product raises an error fastFindKNN(pca, k = 15, metric = "dot_product", type = "knn") #> Error in `.validate_knn_scalars()`: #> ! 'dot_product' is not a proper metric and cannot be used with type='knn' (VP-tree exact search). Use type='ann', or switch to metric='euclidean' or metric='cosine' for exact search.

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: need neighbor indices (e.g. graph construction), set get.distance = FALSE. avoids allocating transmitting n × k distance matrix, saving roughly 50 % output parsing time: fastMakeSNNGraph() fastMakeKNNGraph() wrappers set get.distance = FALSE internally.
code: nn_idx <- fastFindKNN(pca, k = 15, get.distance = FALSE) is.null(nn_idx$distance)   # TRUE #> [1] TRUE

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: Use recall quality matters raw speed — example producing KNN graph underpin publication’s cluster assignments trajectory analysis:
code: nn_highrecall <- fastFindKNN(     pca, k = 15,     M                 = 32L,     ef.search         = 150L,     oversample.factor = 2.0 ) dim(nn_highrecall$index) #> [1] 300  15

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: Product Quantization (PQ) compresses vectors compact codes distance computation, yielding 4–8× search speedup negligible recall loss. Set pq.subspaces ncol(X) / 2 starting point; value must evenly divide ncol(X). small matrices (< 1K rows) JVM startup cost dominates PQ show wall-clock benefit. speedup becomes material n ≥ 10K. Avoid PQ ncol(X) small (< 8 features): quantisation error dominates recall drops sharply. timing comparison large data:
code: # 300 × 20 matrix — use 10 PQ subspaces (= 20 / 2) set.seed(1) pca20 <- matrix(rnorm(300 * 20), 300, 20)  nn_default <- fastFindKNN(pca20, k = 15)                      # no PQ nn_pq      <- fastFindKNN(pca20, k = 15, pq.subspaces = 10L)  # PQ enabled  # Recall overlap (fraction of PQ neighbors that match the default) shared <- mapply(function(a, b) length(intersect(a, b)),                     split(nn_default$index, row(nn_default$index)),                     split(nn_pq$index,      row(nn_pq$index))) message(sprintf("Mean PQ recall vs. default: %.1f%%", 100 * mean(shared / 15))) #> Mean PQ recall vs. default: 100.0% # Illustrative — run on your own large matrix nn_default_time <- system.time(fastFindKNN(large_pca, k = 15)) nn_pq_time <- system.time(     fastFindKNN(large_pca, k = 15,                 pq.subspaces = ncol(large_pca) %/% 2L) ) nn_default_time["elapsed"] / nn_pq_time["elapsed"]  # expect 4–8×

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: jvecfor auto-detects number physical cores uses max(1, physical_cores − 1) threads default. Override num.threads: shared HPC nodes, set num.threads explicitly avoid consuming physical cores interfering co-located jobs.
code: # Single-threaded (reproducible, good for shared HPC nodes) nn_1t <- fastFindKNN(pca, k = 15, num.threads = 1L)  # Explicit thread count nn_4t <- fastFindKNN(pca, k = 15, num.threads = 4L)  # Use verbose to confirm the thread count jvecfor actually uses nn_v <- fastFindKNN(pca, k = 15, num.threads = 2L, verbose = TRUE)

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: fastMakeSNNGraph() fastMakeKNNGraph() wrappers build igraph objects directly PC matrix, combining fastFindKNN() bluster’s graph constructors.

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: snn.type argument controls edge weights computed:
code: library(igraph) #>  #> Attaching package: 'igraph' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     decompose, spectrum #> The following object is masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     union  g_snn <- fastMakeSNNGraph(pca, k = 15) class(g_snn) #> [1] "igraph" igraph::vcount(g_snn)   # 300 — one vertex per cell #> [1] 300 igraph::ecount(g_snn)   # weighted undirected edges #> [1] 34458 g_rank    <- fastMakeSNNGraph(pca, k = 15, snn.type = "rank") g_jaccard <- fastMakeSNNGraph(pca, k = 15, snn.type = "jaccard") g_number  <- fastMakeSNNGraph(pca, k = 15, snn.type = "number")  # Edge weight ranges differ between types summary(igraph::E(g_rank)$weight) #>      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max.  #>  0.000001  6.500000  9.000000  8.707383 11.000000 14.500000 summary(igraph::E(g_jaccard)$weight) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #> 0.03226 0.03226 0.06667 0.07545 0.10345 0.45455

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
code: # Undirected KNN graph (mutual edges) g_knn_u <- fastMakeKNNGraph(pca, k = 15, directed = FALSE)  # Directed KNN graph (each cell points to its k neighbors) g_knn_d <- fastMakeKNNGraph(pca, k = 15, directed = TRUE)  igraph::is_directed(g_knn_d)  # TRUE #> [1] TRUE

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: SNN graph standard input graph-based clustering single-cell analysis. use Louvain algorithm: Leiden clustering (available via igraph ≥ 1.3) gives finer control community resolution:
code: louvain <- igraph::cluster_louvain(g_snn) message(     "Number of detected communities: ",     length(igraph::communities(louvain)) ) #> Number of detected communities: 4 membership_vec <- igraph::membership(louvain) table(membership_vec) #> membership_vec #>  1  2  3  4  #> 36 98 70 96 leiden <- igraph::cluster_leiden(g_snn, resolution_parameter = 0.5) table(igraph::membership(leiden))

title: jvecfor: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: end--end example simulates three cell populations (clusters) embedded 30 PCs recovers via SNN graph clustering. steps use jvecfor igraph. Louvain clusters (colours) PC1-PC2 space. Three well-separated populations recovered.
code: # Simulate 300 cells (100 per cluster) with separable cluster centres in PC1–PC2 set.seed(42) n_per <- 100 centres <- list(c(5, 0), c(-5, 0), c(0, 5))  pca_clust <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(centres), function(i) {     m        <- matrix(rnorm(n_per * 30), n_per, 30)     m[, 1]   <- m[, 1] + centres[[i]][1]     m[, 2]   <- m[, 2] + centres[[i]][2]     m })) true_labels <- rep(1:3, each = n_per) # Step 1: find 15 nearest neighbours nn_wf <- fastFindKNN(pca_clust, k = 15) # Step 2: build SNN graph g_wf <- fastMakeSNNGraph(pca_clust, k = 15) # Step 3: Louvain community detection lou_wf   <- igraph::cluster_louvain(g_wf) detected <- igraph::membership(lou_wf)  # Step 4: cross-tabulate detected vs. true labels print(table(Detected = detected, True = true_labels)) #>         True #> Detected   1   2   3 #>        1  99   0   0 #>        2   1   0 100 #>        3   0 100   0 # Visualise in the first two PCs (base R — no extra dependencies) cluster_cols <- c("#E64B35", "#4DBBD5", "#00A087", "#3C5488", "#F39B7F") plot(     pca_clust[, 1], pca_clust[, 2],     col  = cluster_cols[detected],     pch  = 19, cex = 0.7,     xlab = "PC 1", ylab = "PC 2",     main = "Louvain clusters on SNN graph" ) legend("topright",         legend = paste("Cluster", sort(unique(detected))),         col    = cluster_cols[sort(unique(detected))],         pch    = 19, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)

title: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search for Single-Cell Analysis
text: fastFindKNN() — drop-replacement BiocNeighbors::findKNN; returns index + distance matrices JvecforParam() — BiocNeighborParam subclass drop-BNPARAM integration scran, scater, etc. fastMakeSNNGraph() — convenience wrapper: KNN → bluster::neighborsToSNNGraph fastMakeKNNGraph() — unweighted KNN graph (upper-triangle sparse) Sparse matrix support — dgCMatrix input written MatrixMarket format, avoiding R-side densification Approximate KNN via HNSW-DiskANN — SIMD-accelerated AVX2/AVX-512 supported CPUs Exact KNN via VP-tree — ground-truth validation small datasets Product Quantization (PQ) — optional ~4–8× search speedup minimal recall loss Fully parallel — index build search use shared ForkJoinPool faster n ≥ 50K BiocNeighbors (Annoy) — ~1.5× 100K, ~2× 500K+ (JVM startup overhead dominates small n)

title: Fast K-Nearest Neighbor Search — fastFindKNN
text: X numeric matrix, data.frame, sparse matrix (Matrix::dgCMatrix) rows = observations, cols = features. Sparse matrices written MatrixMarket format densified Java backend, avoiding R-side memory allocation full dense matrix. k Integer. Number nearest neighbors find (excluding self). Default 15. type Character. "ann" approximate (HNSW-DiskANN) "knn" exact (VP-tree). Default "ann". metric Character. Distance metric: "euclidean", "cosine", "dot_product". Default "euclidean". Note: "dot_product" valid type = "ann"; proper metric used VP-tree exact search. num.threads Integer NULL. Number Java threads. NULL, defaults BiocParallel::bpworkers(BPPARAM). BPPARAM BiocParallelParam object controlling thread count. Defaults bpparam(). ef.search Integer. HNSW-DiskANN beam width override (0 = auto: max(k+1, 3k)). meaningful type = "ann". Default 0L. M Integer. HNSW-DiskANN maximum connections per node. Higher values (e.g. 32) improve recall high-dimensional data cost memory slower build. meaningful type = "ann". Default 16L. oversample.factor Numeric. Oversampling multiplier ANN beam width. > 1.0, fetches ceil(ef * oversample.factor) candidates returns top k, improving recall proportional cost. meaningful type = "ann". Default 1.0. pq.subspaces Integer. Number Product Quantization subspaces approximate ANN scoring (0 = disabled). Typical value: ncol(X) / 2. Reduces search time approximately 4-8x minimal recall loss. meaningful type = "ann". Default 0L. get.distance Logical. Return distance matrix alongside index? Default TRUE. verbose Logical. Pass --verbose Java process, enabling HNSW-DiskANN build progress logging stderr. Overrides jvecfor.verbose global option set explicitly. Default getOption("jvecfor.verbose", FALSE).
